unterschrift.text: , Black to move. Red: White attacks b5, the base of the b5–c4 chain.

fragen.frage: Why does White aim at the pawn on b5 with 4. a4?
antworten: Otherwise the pawn on a4 would be lost itself.
b5 is the base of the b5–c4 chain: if b5 falls, c4 loses its support.
White is preparing to castle queenside.
fragen.erklaerung: You attack a pawn chain at its base. Black now has to spend time holding b5.

unterschrift.text: : Black is to move. Gray: the undefended rook on a8 and the pawn on c6, which blocks the a8–f3 diagonal. Red: the queen's path to f3.

fragen.frage: Why is 5... cxb5 a serious mistake here?
antworten: The pawn on c6 opens the a8–f3 diagonal: Qf3 attacks the undefended rook on a8.
The rook on a1 recaptures on b5.
After cxb5, White mates at once.
fragen.erklaerung: The pawn on c6 stood as a barrier between the rook and the diagonal. If you use it to capture, you open the way for your opponent yourself.

unterschrift.text: . Red: queen and king stand on the open e-file.

fragen.frage: Why is the open e-file so dangerous for Black?
antworten: The white king can join the attack via the e-file.
The bishop on c4 gives check on e8 via the e-file.
Queen and king stand one behind the other: a rook on e1 pins the queen to the king.
fragen.erklaerung: An open file in front of your own king is an invitation to the enemy rooks. That is why the king belongs in safety early.

unterschrift.text: , White to move. Black is two pawns up, but the d-file is open.

fragen.frage: Why is 6. Be3 a good move?
antworten: It defends the pawn on d4.
It attacks the queen on d4 and prepares to castle queenside; the d-file is already open.
It threatens mate on f7 at once.
fragen.erklaerung: For two pawns, White has time and open lines. Every further queen move by Black gives White a tempo for development.

unterschrift.text: : Black is to move. Gray: the open d-file. Red: the knight can go to c7 via b5.

fragen.frage: Why is 7... Bg4 a serious mistake?
antworten: It does attack the queen on f3, but after Nb5 White threatens Nxc7 mate, and winning the queen comes too late.
The bishop on g4 is undefended and is lost at once.
With Bg4, Black loses the right to castle.
fragen.erklaerung: White answers 8. Nb5!! and leaves the queen where it is. The king on e8 has no square; the rook on d1 covers d7 and d8.

fragen.frage: Why can't Black take the queen on f3?
antworten: Because White then mates with Nxc7, no matter how much material Black wins first.
Because the bishop on g4 is pinned to the king.
Because the queen on b4 is then attacked by the bishop on e3.

fragen.frage: Why is 6. Nxd5 a mistake, even though the knight on f6 is pinned?
antworten: The pawn on d5 is defended by the bishop on f8.
The pawn on e6 recaptures the knight on d5.
The pin is only relative: Black recaptures, gives up the queen and wins it back with Bb4+.

fragen.frage: Why is 5... Bh5 dangerous?
antworten: On h5 the bishop is undefended and is captured by the queen on d1.
White plays 6. Nxe5 and offers the queen: if Black takes it, mate follows with Bxf7+ and Nd5.
After Bh5, Black can no longer castle.
fragen.erklaerung: The pin only seemed to hold the knight on f3 in place. After 6. Nxe5!! Bxd1 7. Bxf7+ Ke7 8. Nd5, Black is mated.

Because the bishop on h5 is pinned to the king.
Because White then wins the queen back at once.
fragen.erklaerung: The king on e7 has no escape square: d7, e6, e8 and f6 are covered. The knight on e5 protects the bishop on f7.

antworten: It defends the pawn on e4.

Because the queen on e2 then no longer defends the pawn on e4.
